description:
Advances: specled.api_boundary

Review-bar-override: seeding-after-detection changes first-run semantics — needs a spec decision + ADR, not an edit.

From the critical review of specled_-n5q (finding F4, Medium, security reviewer).

Seeding runs BEFORE detection and is not divergence-gated, so a run against a stale or cold _build can write an entry labeled resolved_via: "source" for a binding that production resolves via beam. Once written, every subsequent run diverges against it — and divergence blocks the refresh, so the entry can never be rewritten. Permanently stuck.

Why it could not land on the release branch: the narrow discriminator (refuse to seed when resolution looks beam-missing) is provably wrong — a legitimate private-function binding and a stale-beam miss both present as "module loaded, function_exported?/3 false, [:beam_fn_missing]". Refusing on that signature would refuse 14 of this repo own 173 entries.

The viable fix is to seed AFTER detection, which changes first-run seeding semantics: the detector currently reads the store post-seed, so a first-run binding produces no finding by construction. That is a spec decision plus an ADR, not an edit.
title: Baseline seeding is not divergence-gated: a stale _build can write a permanently-stuck source label
